# An interval from two two-limb numbers

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `interval_make_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The interval of two values of `T`; the whole line when a bound is a NaN or both are the same infinity, and the empty set when they are reversed:

$$Z = [l_o, h_i].$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $l_o = l_{o0} + l_{o1}$, $h_i = h_{i0} + h_{i1}$, $z_l = z_{l0} + z_{l1}$, $z_u = z_{u0} + z_{u1}$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Interval<T, 2>(lo, hi)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | `Interval<T, 2>` | implicit for one operand; `constexpr`; does not round |
| `Interval<T, 2>(lo, hi)` | `T`, `T` | `Interval<T, 2>` | each value of `T` converted to `Expansion<T, 2>` first, exactly (`make_2`); `constexpr`; does not round |
| `Interval<T, 2>(a)` | `T` | `Interval<T, 2>` | implicit; $l_o = h_i = a$, each value of `T` converted to `Expansion<T, 2>` first, exactly (`make_2`); `constexpr`; does not round |
| `Interval<T, 2>(a)` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | `Interval<T, 2>` | implicit; $l_o = h_i = a$; `constexpr`; does not round |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $l_o$ is canonical: finite and normalized, or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$, or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.
- $h_i$ is canonical: finite and normalized, or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$, or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result $Z = [z_l, z_u]$ is a canonical interval.
- If a bound is a NaN, whatever the other, or both are the same infinity ($[+\infty, +\infty]$, $[-\infty, -\infty]$): $Z$ is the whole line, $[-\infty, +\infty]$.
- Otherwise, if the bounds are reversed, $l_o > h_i$ ($[+\infty, -\infty]$, and $l_o = +\infty$ or $h_i = -\infty$ with the other finite, among them): $Z$ is the empty set, $(+\infty, -\infty)$.
- Otherwise ($l_o \le h_i$, $l_o < +\infty$ and $h_i > -\infty$): $Z$ is $[l_o, h_i]$, the same extended real numbers (a zero may change its sign).

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `interval_make_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalExact.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalExact.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions interval_make_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `interval_make_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** constructor of an interval of two limbs (Milestone 2 listing; equal infinities the whole line, 2026-11-20). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_make_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_make_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`le_2_2`](le_2_2.md), [`lt_2_2`](lt_2_2.md).

```
# An interval from two canonical 2-limb values (milestone2.md, "Interval kernels", "Values of an
# interval"): the listing of interval_make_1 on the comparisons of two limbs, le_2_2 and lt_2_2 for
# the order of the bounds and the leading limbs for the tests against infinity (a canonical NaN is
# all NaN, and a comparison with it is false). The values are limbs of objects, already canonical,
# so nothing is guarded. The whole line when a bound is a NaN, whatever the other bound is, and when
# both bounds are the same infinity (decided on 2026-11-20, as for interval_make_1); otherwise the
# empty set when lo > hi (rv); otherwise [lo, hi], an infinite bound returned as (+-inf, 0). For
# every precision.

ok  = le_2_2(lo0, lo1, hi0, hi1)
nl  = lt(lo0, const inf)
mi  = neg(const inf)
nu  = lt(mi, hi0)
va  = and(ok, nl)
v   = and(va, nu)
rv  = lt_2_2(hi0, hi1, lo0, lo1)
el  = select(rv, const inf, mi)
eu  = select(rv, mi, const inf)
zl0 = select(v, lo0, el)
zl1 = select(v, lo1, 0)
zu0 = select(v, hi0, eu)
zu1 = select(v, hi1, 0)
```
